LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LEARN

Welcome to an English program for grade four. Today, we are going to learn the use of full stops and capital letters as punctuation marks. Your teacher is Joyce Agik. Learner, can you write your name and the name of your parent? Write your name and the name of your parent. - Well done. Did you write your name starting with a Capital letter? - Say the following sentences after me. Tina would like to visit Mombasa. - Jonah would like to visit Kitale. - Well done learner. Did you notice that the sentences contain names of people and places? Names of people, places and things are called NOUNS. Specific names of people, places, days of the week, months of the year and features like mountains and rivers are called PROPER NOUNS. Specific names of people, places, days of the week, months of the year and features like mountains and rivers are called PROPER NOUNS. Learner, can you say proper nouns? - Good learner. All proper nouns begin with a capital letter. Sentences also begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

Learner, give me examples of names of people. - Good learner. Now, give me examples of names or places like towns and counties. - Very good learner. Can you give examples of names of rivers and mountains? - Well done, learner. Now listen to the following examples of proper nouns. Names of people. Number one Chebet. Number two Kamau. Number three, James. And number four, Bakari. Names of place. One, Nairobi. Two Mombasa. Three, Kericho. Four Kakamega. Names of rivers and mountains. One River Tana. Two River Athi. Three. Mount Kenya. And for Mount Elgon. Well, learner, all these are examples of proper nouns, and they start with capital letters. Do you know how many days are there in a week? - Write down the names of the days of the week. Remember, they should begin with capital letters. - Very good. The days of the week are. Sunday. Monday. Tuesday. Wednesday. Thursday. Friday and Saturday. They are all proper nouns. Learner, I want you to identify proper nouns in the following sentences. One. Luke went to the cyber on Monday. Luke went to the cyber on Monday - Two. Jane is using the internet to learn. Jane is using the internet to learn. Three, our school visited Mount Kenya on Friday. Our school visited Mount Kenya on Friday. - And four. Tina would like to go to River Tana. Tina would like to go to River Tana. -

Very good, Learner. The answers are. One. The proper nouns are. Luke and Monday. Number two, the proper noun is Jane. Number three, the proper nouns. Mount Kenya and Friday. And number four. The proper nouns are Tina and River Tina. Learner. Write down the following sentences in your exercise book. Make sure you start the sentences with capital letters and end in full stop. Remember to write all proper nouns, beginning with a capital letter. Number one. Rita went to River Nyando on Wednesday. Rita went to River Nyando on Wednesday. - Number two, I climbed Mount Kenya with my friend Rhoda. I climbed Mount Kenya with my friend Rhoda. - Number three. Every Sunday, we go to church. Every Sunday, we go to church. - And number four, my uncle lives in Kisumu. My uncle lives in Kisumu. - Learner, share your work with your parent or guardian to find out whether you have used the correct punctuation. Share your work with your parent or guardian to find out whether you have used the correct punctuation. Thank you learner. In our lesson today we have learned that. One sentence should start with capital letters and end in full stop. Number two, proper nouns are specific names of people, places, days of the week, months of the year, features like mountains and rivers. They all start with capital letters. - Your radio teacher was Joyce Agik. The program was written and produced by the It was recorded by John Mbithi for the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development. Until next time. Goodbye.

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation
2. Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
3. Learning materials: ENGLISH_GRADE_4___PROG_8 full stops and capital letters
4. Revise with the quiz now.
